summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease, was admitted for hyperkalemia and acute on chronic kidney injury with creatinine rising to 3.2 from a baseline of 2.2. The etiology was thought to be multifactorial, including recent uptitration of Lasix, decreased oral intake, and possible intravascular depletion. He received kayexelate prior to admission, and his potassium normalized. IV albumin was given for volume support. His creatinine improved to 2.9 by discharge. He was managed with holding diuresis, low-sodium diet, and compression stockings for chronic leg edema. His myeloma treatment with carfilzomib was held during admission and planned for resumption post-discharge. Pancytopenia persisted but remained stable without transfusion. Insulin was adjusted due to hypoglycemia at home, and Tresiba was restarted at discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged with nephrology and oncology.
